title: Novena for Passing an Exam
kicker: 9 days of wisdom, diligence and peace
card: For anyone preparing for an important exam: 9 days asking for wisdom, diligence, a calm mind and trust in God’s will.
ogDescription: 9 days of prayer for passing an exam, through Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, St. Joseph of Cupertino and St. Thomas Aquinas.
description: A 9-day Catholic novena before a board exam, bar exam or finals, through Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, St. Joseph of Cupertino and St. Thomas Aquinas.

epigraph.text: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me; I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

closingVerse.text: I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will counsel you with my eye upon you.

saints.name: St. Joseph of Cupertino
saints.patron: Patron of students & those taking exams
saints.bio: Franciscan friar from Copertino in southern Italy who struggled with learning, yet was ordained a priest and became known for his ecstasies in prayer. Canonized in 1767.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Joseph of Cupertino lifted in prayer, by Placido Costanzi

saints.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
saints.bio: Dominican friar and theologian, author of the Summa Theologiae and of hymns for Corpus Christi. A Doctor of the Church, named patron of Catholic schools by Pope Leo XIII in 1880.
saints.alt: Painting: St. Thomas Aquinas holding a church and a book, by Carlo Crivelli
saints.openingRole: teacher who prayed before he studied

openingPrayer: Heavenly Father, You know the exam that N. is preparing for: the long hours of study, the pressure and the hopes that rest on it, and the worry of all who love them. We place this exam in Your hands, and we trust in Your care more than in our fear. Give N. diligence, a clear mind and an honest heart, and let Your will be done. Today we ask Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom; St. Joseph of Cupertino, friend of struggling students; and St. Thomas Aquinas, who prayed before he studied, to join their prayers with ours before Your throne, through Christ our Lord.
closingPrayer: Lord Jesus, Wisdom of the Father, bless N. as they prepare and on the day of the exam. Give them a clear mind, an honest heart and peace in Your holy will, whatever the result.

tips.p: One person leads each part; all respond pray for us and Amen, and say the closing prayers together. The prayers say “we”; if you pray alone, say “I”.

If you can, go to Confession and attend Mass during these 9 days, and receive Communion before the exam. Pair prayer with good preparation: a study plan (Day 4), enough sleep (Day 5), and no leaked questions, copied answers or fixers (Day 6). If the result is not what you hoped, be gentle with yourself and others; many pass on a retake. If worry or disappointment becomes too heavy to carry, talk to someone you trust: a parent, a priest or a counselor. At “N.”, say the student’s name; if you are praying for yourself, say “me”.

intentionPlaceholder: Write the name of the student, the exam and its date, and the graces you ask.
credits: Images: Carlo Crivelli, St Thomas Aquinas, 1476, National Gallery, London · Placido Costanzi, A Miracle of Saint Joseph of Cupertino, 1750, Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York · Bartolomeo Montagna, Madonna Enthroned (detail), 1500. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

days.title: Honest About Our Worry
days.verse: For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; it is I who say to you, “Fear not, I will help you.”
days.refl: Before an important exam, worry can sit like a weight on the chest: review notes that never seem to end, the cost of school and review fees, the fear of letting down the people who sacrificed for us. God does not scold us for that fear. He takes our right hand, the very hand that will hold the pen, and says, “Fear not, I will help you.” We begin these nine days by telling Him honestly how we feel.
days.more: St. Joseph of Cupertino knew what it was to feel slow and behind. As a young man in Copertino, in southern Italy, he struggled with his studies and found learning hard. Yet God drew him close. He became a Franciscan friar and a priest, so absorbed in prayer that he was known for his ecstasies. He is a friend to every student who fears they are not clever enough.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, You know N. by name, and You know how heavy this exam feels for them and for all of us who love them. We are anxious, and we tell You so. Take N. by the hand, as You promised, and quiet the fear that makes it hard to think. Through the prayers of Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, St. Joseph of Cupertino and St. Thomas Aquinas, give N. the courage to keep going, one day and one page at a time.
days.step: Write the name of the exam and its date on a card, and keep it where you pray these nine days.

days.title: Offering Our Work to God
days.verse: Commit your work to the LORD, / and your plans will be established.
days.refl: Studying can feel like a lonely race against the calendar. Proverbs offers another way: commit the work to the Lord. That does not mean we stop studying and wait for a miracle. It means every hour at the desk, every practice test and every chapter read again can be offered to God as an act of love. When our work is placed in His hands, it is no longer ours alone, and the outcome rests with Him too.
days.more: St. Thomas Aquinas was one of the greatest minds the Church has known, yet it is said that he never began to study or write without first praying. A prayer before study long attributed to him, still used by students, asks the Creator of all things to guide the beginning of their work, direct its progress and bring it to completion. Prayer did not replace his study; it gave his study its direction.
days.prayer: Lord God, we commit this exam and all the work before it into Your hands. Bless every hour of study, every review class and every practice test, and make them an offering of love to You. Through the prayers of St. Thomas Aquinas, who began his study with prayer, and of Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, and St. Joseph of Cupertino, help N. work faithfully today and leave tomorrow, and the results, in Your care.
days.step: Before you study today, offer the hour to God in a short prayer of your own, or pray St. Thomas Aquinas’s prayer before study.

days.title: Asking for Wisdom
days.verse: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all men generously and without reproaching, and it will be given him.
days.refl: St. James makes a remarkable promise: ask God for wisdom, and He will give it generously, without making us feel foolish for asking. Wisdom is more than memorizing facts. It is understanding what we learn, seeing how things fit together, and knowing what matters most. Today we ask boldly for that gift, and for the help we need now: understanding as we study, a memory that keeps what we have learned, and good judgment to use it well, now and in the work ahead.
days.more: In the Litany of Loreto the Church calls Mary the Seat of Wisdom. Christ, the Wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24), rested in her arms as a child, as a king sits on his throne. Mary kept the events of His childhood and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). She shows us that true wisdom begins in a heart that listens to God, and she brings our prayers for understanding to her Son.
days.prayer: God of all wisdom, You give generously to all who ask. We ask You now for N.: understanding as they study, a memory that holds what they learn, and the judgment to use it well. With Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, who held Your eternal Word in her arms, and with St. Thomas Aquinas and St. Joseph of Cupertino praying for us, open N.’s mind to the truth and keep their heart humble and teachable.
days.step: Pray one Hail Mary before each study session today, asking Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, for understanding.

days.title: Diligence in Study
days.verse: Whatever your task, work heartily, as serving the Lord and not men, knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward; you are serving the Lord Christ.
days.refl: Prayer is not a shortcut around study. God usually answers our prayer for a good exam through the ordinary work of preparation: reading carefully, reviewing faithfully, practicing until things become clear. St. Paul asks us to work heartily, as serving the Lord. That turns study into a kind of service. On tired days, when distractions call and the material feels endless, we can remember that even this quiet, hidden effort is offered to Christ, who sees it all.
days.more: The story is told that when St. Joseph of Cupertino came to his examination for the diaconate, there was only one passage of the Gospel he knew well, and he was asked to explain that very text. For this reason, students have long asked his prayers before exams. The story is not a promise that we can skip our studies. It reminds us that God sees both our honest effort and our limits.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You worked with Your hands at Nazareth and did each task with love. Give N. diligence in study: the discipline to keep a good schedule, the focus to set distractions aside, and the perseverance to keep going on tired days. Through the prayers of St. Joseph of Cupertino, who knew how hard learning can be, and of Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, and St. Thomas Aquinas, make every hour of study a gift offered to You.
days.step: Make a simple study plan for the days until the exam, and put your phone in another room for one study session today.

days.title: Rest for Body & Mind
days.verse: It is in vain that you rise up early / and go late to rest, / eating the bread of anxious toil; / for he gives to his beloved sleep.
days.refl: Many of us know the all-night cram, fueled by coffee and fear. The psalm gently says it is in vain. God does not want us to wear ourselves out as if everything depended on us alone. Sleep is not wasted time: it helps the mind keep what we have studied, and going to bed on time is a small act of trust. Today we pray for rest and health during review season, and on the night before the exam.
days.more: St. Thomas Aquinas taught that the mind, like the body, needs rest, and that wholesome recreation has a place in a virtuous life. He even retold an old story of St. John the Evangelist, who relaxed with his disciples and explained that a bow kept always bent will break. Good meals, a short walk, time with friends and a full night’s sleep are part of good preparation, not a lack of seriousness.
days.prayer: Loving Father, You give Your beloved sleep. Protect N. from exhaustion and from the anxious toil that wears down body and mind. Grant them good health, restful nights, and the wisdom to stop studying when it is time to rest. With St. Thomas Aquinas, who taught that the mind needs rest, and with Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, and St. Joseph of Cupertino praying for us, renew N.’s strength each morning.
days.step: Tonight, set a time to stop studying, put away screens, and pray a short night prayer before you sleep.

days.title: Integrity Without Shortcuts
days.verse: He who walks in integrity walks securely, / but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
days.refl: Under pressure, shortcuts can look tempting: leaked questions, a classmate’s answers, a hidden note, a fixer who promises a sure pass. Proverbs says that whoever walks in integrity walks securely. An honest result, whatever it is, is worth more than a dishonest pass. One day patients, clients, students and whole communities will trust what this exam says we know. Today we pray for the grace and the courage to keep our hands and hearts clean, whatever it costs.
days.more: Cheating harms more than the one who cheats. It wrongs classmates who studied honestly and the people who will one day depend on our knowledge. Honesty also frees us: we can walk into the exam room with a clear conscience, knowing that whatever happens is truly ours. If we have cut corners before, the door of mercy is open in Confession, and God’s grace can make us people others can trust.
days.prayer: Lord, You are the Truth. Keep N. honest in study and in the exam room. Free them from every temptation to cheat, to copy or to buy an easy way through, and give them the courage to refuse when others do not. Through the prayers of St. Joseph of Cupertino, humble and simple before You, and of Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, and St. Thomas Aquinas, let N.’s results, whatever they are, be honestly their own.
days.step: Decide now that you will not use leaked questions or copied answers, and tell God so in a short prayer.

days.title: Peace on Exam Day
days.verse: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid.
days.refl: Jesus spoke these words on the night before His Passion, when His friends were frightened. He did not promise them an easy tomorrow; He gave them His own peace. On exam day, that peace is what we need most: a calm heart, a clear mind, and the steadiness to read each question carefully. When panic rises or the mind goes blank, we can breathe slowly, whisper His name, and go on calmly to the next question.
days.more: A few simple habits help peace take root: preparing documents, pencils and the route the night before, leaving early, eating something, and arriving with time to pray. Some students hold a small rosary or pray a Hail Mary as they sit down. These are not lucky charms; they help us remember that we are not alone in the exam room. Christ is there, and so are the prayers of all who love us.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, give N. Your peace on the day of the exam. Calm their nerves, clear their mind, and help them read every question carefully and answer with confidence. If panic rises or memory fails, steady them and bring back what they have learned. With Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, St. Joseph of Cupertino and St. Thomas Aquinas praying beside them, let N. do their best with a quiet heart.
days.step: Prepare everything for exam day the night before, and choose a short prayer to say as you sit down, such as “Jesus, I trust in You.”

days.title: Gifts Meant for Others
days.verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.
days.refl: An exam is never only about a score. Behind every board exam, bar exam or entrance exam there is a calling: the nurse who will care for the sick, the engineer whose bridges people will cross, the teacher who will form children, the lawyer who will defend the weak. Jesus asks us to let our light shine through good works that give glory to the Father. Today we pray that all this learning may one day become service.
days.more: St. Thomas Aquinas did not study for his own glory. Near the end of his life, after an experience during Mass, he stopped writing, and said that all he had written seemed like straw compared with what he had seen. He never despised learning; he saw it in its true place, at the service of God and neighbor. Our diplomas and licenses, too, are gifts to be shared, not trophies to keep.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, every gift of mind and heart comes from You. We pray that N.’s studies may become a light for others in the work You are calling them to. Make them competent, honest and compassionate toward everyone who will depend on them. Through the prayers of St. Thomas Aquinas, who placed all his learning at Your service, and of Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, and St. Joseph of Cupertino, let their work give You glory.
days.step: Write one sentence about the people you hope to serve through the work this exam opens, and keep it with your notes.

days.title: Gratitude & Trust in God’s Will
days.verse: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, / and do not rely on your own insight. / In all your ways acknowledge him, / and he will make straight your paths.
days.refl: We end these nine days by trusting in the Lord with all our heart, not relying on our own insight. We have studied, prayed and asked boldly. Now we give thanks, because God has heard every prayer and will make straight our paths. A pass is a gift to receive with gratitude. If the result is not what we hoped, it is not a sign that God has abandoned us or that our prayer was weak. His care for us has not changed.
days.more: Many good nurses, engineers, teachers and lawyers did not pass on their first try. If you or someone you love must retake an exam, there is no shame in it. Grieve honestly, rest, and then begin again, perhaps with a new plan. Be gentle with those who did not pass: a kind word or a shared meal can mean more than advice. And whatever the result, give thanks for the graces of these days.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, on this ninth day we thank You for Your faithfulness and for every grace, seen and unseen, that You have given N. in these days of study and prayer. Thank you, Our Lady, Seat of Wisdom, St. Joseph of Cupertino and St. Thomas Aquinas, for carrying our prayers before Jesus. We entrust this exam, its results and N.’s whole future to Your loving will, trusting that You will lead them in the way that is truly good.
days.step: Write down three graces you noticed during these nine days, and thank God for them together.

printClosing: I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go;
I will counsel you with my eye upon you.
